articles.title: Mayor announces plan to rename Times Square “New Red Square”
articles.deck: Citing “vibes,” the mayor pitched the change at a 7 a.m. press conference held inside a Sbarro.
articles.author: Helena Park
articles.excerpt: Standing beneath a flickering Pepsi sign, the mayor unveiled a sweeping rebrand that several officials confirmed they had not been told about.
articles.body:
Standing beneath a flickering Pepsi sign, the mayor unveiled a sweeping rebrand that several officials confirmed they had not been told about.

The announcement, delivered to a small but visibly confused crowd of tourists who had been promised a free pretzel, marks the most aggressive municipal naming initiative since the rebrand of the Bronx as “The Bronx, But Like, Newer.”

## What we know so far

> “We considered every option. We then picked the one we'd already decided on. That's leadership.”

A senior aide called the proposal “a return to common sense, by which we mean the version of common sense that polls best.” Charts were shown. The charts were not, strictly speaking, related to anything.

## Reaction has been mixed

Local merchants reached for comment expressed cautious optimism, by which they appeared to mean cautious nothing. One bakery owner, holding what could only be described as a defensive croissant, said the changes would not affect her in any way she could think of, and asked us to please leave.

articles.title: Kegel USA set to take over NYC Armory in one of the strangest competitions on record
articles.deck: Organizers promise “dignified intensity” and a souvenir tote bag at the door.
articles.author: Margaux Tilden
articles.excerpt: Tickets sold out in under nine minutes, prompting a statement from the venue asking attendees to please remain calm and seated.
articles.body:
Tickets sold out in under nine minutes, prompting a statement from the venue asking attendees to please remain calm and seated.

The Park Avenue Armory, traditionally home to contemporary art installations and the occasional society fundraiser, will play host this June to what organizers describe — without elaboration — as “the most important domestic floor-based competition of the calendar year.”

## A serious sport, allegedly

Kegel USA, an organization that no fewer than three reporters could not locate online prior to publication, says the event will feature regional champions from “most or all of the lower 48 states.” A spokesperson declined to confirm whether spectators would be permitted to applaud.

articles.title: Trump downplays China trip, calls it basically a short holiday with CEOs
articles.deck: “Mostly snacks, some hats,” the former president said while boarding a private jet bound for a different jet.
articles.author: Devin Royce
articles.excerpt: Aides described the itinerary as “flexible to the point of theoretical,” adding that several meetings would be conducted entirely in mime.
articles.body:
Aides described the itinerary as “flexible to the point of theoretical,” adding that several meetings would be conducted entirely in mime.

The former president, asked Tuesday whether the trip had any policy implications, paused for roughly nine seconds before answering “sure.”

## The official explanation

According to two staffers granted anonymity because they had already been quoted by name in a different outlet earlier in the day, the visit consists of three meals, one ribbon-cutting, and a “meaningful walk.” The walk will be observed but not filmed.

articles.title: Inside BabyMaxxing, fashion’s most unsettling new youth aesthetic
articles.deck: Bonnets are back, allegedly on purpose.
articles.author: Iris Halloran
articles.excerpt: A generation raised on screens has, against all advice, decided to dress like the cast of an oil painting about teething.
articles.body:
A generation raised on screens has, against all advice, decided to dress like the cast of an oil painting about teething.

The trend, which began in late winter on a single TikTok account belonging to a graduate student who has since deleted it, involves what proponents describe as “strategic infantilization” and what dermatologists describe as “concerning, please stop.”

## How it works

A proper BabyMaxx outfit requires, at minimum, one bonnet, two pairs of socks worn over jeans, a teething ring used as a bracelet, and what the community calls “a confused expression.” The look is finished with a small spoon.

articles.title: Joe Rogan’s latest health hack? 18 ounces of breastmilk a day
articles.deck: His doctor declined to comment, then declined a second time, more firmly.
articles.author: Sam Albright
articles.excerpt: The podcaster described the routine as “surprisingly portable,” a phrase that listeners are encouraged not to dwell on.
articles.body:
The podcaster described the routine as “surprisingly portable,” a phrase that listeners are encouraged not to dwell on.

In an episode that ran longer than several feature films, the host explained that the regimen — which he called a “stack” — was inspired by an unspecified conversation with a man at a sauna.

articles.title: Senate quietly debates a bill that would give pigeons standing in small claims court
articles.deck: Several senators support the measure; none can fully explain why.
articles.author: Helena Park
articles.excerpt: A floor speech delivered entirely in coos was met with applause and at least one standing ovation from the press gallery.
articles.body:
A floor speech delivered entirely in coos was met with applause and at least one standing ovation from the press gallery.

The bill, S. 4412, would extend limited legal standing to “any urban-adjacent columbiform” in disputes involving food theft, statue damage, and what the text calls “sustained eye contact.”

articles.title: Cow elected to town board in narrow upset; sworn in over the weekend
articles.deck: Officials say the cow “seems to be settling in,” though some questions remain about quorum.
articles.author: Margaux Tilden
articles.excerpt: The cow’s campaign focused on infrastructure, transparency, and a vague but persistent interest in the high school baseball field.
articles.body:
The cow’s campaign focused on infrastructure, transparency, and a vague but persistent interest in the high school baseball field.

Voter turnout for the off-cycle election was the highest the town clerk could remember, citing what she called “a very particular kind of curiosity.”

articles.title: Sundance to ban phones from screenings, theaters, lobbies, and ideally minds
articles.deck: Festival organizers say enforcement will be “social, not legal.”
articles.author: Iris Halloran
articles.excerpt: Attendees will be issued a small notebook and a single short pencil, sharpened only on arrival.
articles.body:
Attendees will be issued a small notebook and a single short pencil, sharpened only on arrival.

The move comes in response to what the festival director described as “a vibe problem,” citing audiences increasingly distracted by their phones, each other’s phones, and a strange new generation of phones that does not yet exist.

articles.title: Wisconsin lake refuses to freeze for fourth winter in a row, blames “personal reasons”
articles.author: Devin Royce
articles.excerpt: The lake released a brief statement through a kayak rental shop, asking only for privacy and a moment to think.
articles.body:
The lake released a brief statement through a kayak rental shop, asking only for privacy and a moment to think.

The news arrives at a fraught moment for area ice fishermen, several of whom have begun listing their equipment on local trading boards under headings such as “Not Bitter, Just Realistic.”

articles.title: Internet collectively decides bread was a mistake; supermarkets remain calm
articles.deck: Bakers report no change in foot traffic; comment sections, however, are in flames.
articles.author: Iris Halloran
articles.excerpt: The shift is being tracked by analysts who specialize in opinions that affect almost nothing.
articles.body:
The shift is being tracked by analysts who specialize in opinions that affect almost nothing.

A viral thread Tuesday catalyzed what one observer called “the most decisive non-event of the spring,” reframing thousands of years of grain cultivation as a “collective lapse in judgment.”

articles.title: Pets across America resign en masse after companies recall workers to the office
articles.deck: A Labrador in Cleveland issued a memo using a single very wet paw.
articles.author: Sam Albright
articles.excerpt: Hamsters and certain especially principled goldfish have begun honoring a quiet, dignified strike.
articles.body:
Hamsters and certain especially principled goldfish have begun honoring a quiet, dignified strike.

The coordinated walk-off, which one parrot described as “overdue,” marks the most visible domestic-animal action since the Great Cat Refusal of 2019.

articles.title: Opinion: Maybe we should just cancel Monday and see what happens
articles.deck: It’s not a serious proposal, except in the ways that it is.
articles.author: Devin Royce
articles.excerpt: We tried four-day weeks. We tried summer Fridays. The data is in: Monday simply does not deliver value to shareholders.
articles.body:
We tried four-day weeks. We tried summer Fridays. The data is in: Monday simply does not deliver value to shareholders.

Monday, frankly, has been coasting on legacy goodwill for two centuries. Sunday is beloved. Friday is essential. Tuesday is functional. Monday is, at best, a placeholder.

This column proposes — modestly, in the long tradition of modest proposals — that we simply skip it. Stop scheduling it. Stop counting it. Let it lapse, like a magazine subscription nobody renewed.
